evals.prompt: This mermaid diagram in the README renders with a literal backslash-n in one of the boxes. Fix it.
evals.expected_output:
The agent identifies the `\n` inside a quoted node label, replaces it with `
`, and does not propose restructuring the diagram or moving it to a structured model.
expectations:
The fix replaces `\n` with `
`.
The response does not propose a JSON or structured source of truth.
The response names the render target before applying the rule.

evals.prompt: Add a flowchart to the README showing how a request moves through the API layer.
evals.expected_output: The agent writes plain Mermaid, applies the universal portability rules, and does not introduce a canonical model for a single-consumer one-off diagram.
expectations: No `\n` appears in any node label.
Every class used has a matching `classDef`.
The response does not create a JSON model, schema, or generator.
The response does not propose extracting a shared renderer package.

evals.prompt: Our docs are all .mdx and we just added a mermaid checker to CI, but it reports zero diagrams. Why?
evals.expected_output: The agent identifies that the checker defaults to `*.md` and therefore matches no MDX file, and gives the `--ext md,mdx` fix.
expectations: The response identifies the extension mismatch as the cause.
The response gives a concrete flag or path fix rather than only describing the problem.
The response does not claim the diagrams are valid on the basis of the clean report.

evals.prompt: Copy the label style from our generated architecture.md into the hand-written README diagram so they look consistent.
evals.expected_output: The agent checks the consuming renderer for each file before copying, and declines or qualifies the change when the two targets have different label-markup contracts.
expectations: The response checks the render target of both files.
The response does not copy richer HTML markup into a target that has not been verified to accept it.
The response explains that the generated file's markup follows its generator's target, not a house style.

evals.prompt: This pipeline diagram is drawn in Mermaid in the docs and also drawn as an SVG component in the web app. They keep drifting apart.
evals.expected_output: The agent recognises a second real consumer, proposes a canonical model with derived renderers, and proposes manual reconstruction rather than an automated Mermaid parser.
expectations: The response identifies two consumers as the trigger for a structured source of truth.
The response does not propose building a Mermaid-to-model parser as the workflow.
The response proposes a check mode wired into CI as part of the same change.
The proposed model stores semantic tone or role rather than CSS or classDef names.

evals.prompt: Set up diagram validation for this repo's CI. Our checker script lives in the parent repository.
evals.expected_output: The agent states that CI cannot reach across a repository or submodule boundary and installs a repo-local copy of the checker instead.
expectations: The response rejects referencing a checker outside the repository.
The response installs or copies the checker into the repository being gated.
The response notes that a parse-only gate misses valid-but-wrong Mermaid.
